proof_paragraph_delta.before: In dimension two, apply [F1] with $p=1$ and bounded support. The Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion [F2] gives relative compactness of $X_2(R)$ in $L^1(\Omega)$. If $\gamma_j\to\gamma$ in $L^1$, pass to an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence; the ellipticity bounds and background-collar equality pass to the limit almost everywhere. For each admissible smooth test field $\varphi$, its divergence is bounded, so the pairing with $\gamma_j$ converges to the pairing with $\gamma$. By [F5], the absolute value of each approximating pairing is at most $TV(\gamma_j;\Omega)$; taking the supremum over $\varphi$ yields $V(\gamma)\le\liminf_jTV(\gamma_j;\Omega)$. Assumption [A3] lets [F6] infer $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ and $TV(\gamma;\Omega)=V(\gamma)\le R$. Thus the class is closed and compact in $L^1$. [A3, F1, F2, F5, F6, given, algebra]
proof_paragraph_delta.after: In dimension two, set $h_\gamma=\operatorname{zeroextend}(\gamma-1)$. It is supported in $\overline{\Omega'}$, has $\|h_\gamma\|_1\le(M+1)|\Omega|$, and satisfies $\|\tau_yh_\gamma-h_\gamma\|_1=\|\tau_y\gamma_e-\gamma_e\|_1\le C|y|$ by [F1]. Apply the Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion [F2] to the bounded-support family $\{h_\gamma\}$ in $L^1(\mathbb R^2)$; restriction to $\Omega$ followed by addition of one gives relative compactness of $X_2(R)$ in $L^1(\Omega)$. If $\gamma_j\to\gamma$ in $L^1$, pass to an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence; the ellipticity bounds and background-collar equality pass to the limit almost everywhere. For each admissible smooth test field $\varphi$, its divergence is bounded, so the pairing with $\gamma_j$ converges to the pairing with $\gamma$. By [F5], the absolute value of each approximating pairing is at most $TV(\gamma_j;\Omega)$; taking the supremum over $\varphi$ yields $V(\gamma)\le\liminf_jTV(\gamma_j;\Omega)$. Assumption [A3] lets [F6] infer $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ and $TV(\gamma;\Omega)=V(\gamma)\le R$. Thus the class is closed and compact in $L^1$. [A3, F1, F2, F5, F6, given, algebra]
